name: base
purpose: default parameters, 5 ns clock. Power-up with tap codes 3/3 and an empty history: the first decision has no feedback and the second uses tap 1 only; a feedback that cancels; decisions that the feedback turns against the raw input. Tap codes change to 2/1 between edges, and the paper example of the decision card: vin = 0.46 V gives low after history (+1, -1) and high after (-1, +1). A reset that rises between edges and spans two edges while the tap codes change to 1/3; the first two decisions after it. vin changes in the middle of every clock interval.

name: history-pairs
purpose: default parameters, 4 ns clock. For six tap-code pairs (1/2, 2/1, 3/0, 0/3, 3/2, 1/3) and each of the four histories, two decisions far from vcm set the history and a probe at vcm +- 5 mV follows, so the same input and taps give different decisions after different histories. Probes decided against the raw input feed the next corrections; the first decision after each tap change uses the new codes with the old history.

name: reset-restart
purpose: tr = 400 ps (100 ps grid, 200 ps control edges), 5 ns clock. rst is high at t = 0 with tap codes 3/2 and two clock edges pass in reset; a 0.502 ns reset pulse between two edges (the 0.5 ns minimum plus a 2 ps design margin, since a separation exactly at a minimum is a tie); a reset across two edges while the codes change to 2/3; a double reset whose second rising crossing finds the outputs cleared; a reset held to the end with two more edges. Each restart is followed by its first and second decisions with nonzero taps.

name: isi-channel
purpose: default parameters, 2.05 ns clock (the shortest legal period of 2 ns plus one 50 ps grid step as a design margin, since a period exactly at the minimum is a tie), tap codes 2/1 matched to a channel with 40 mV and 20 mV post-cursors: vin = vcm + 50 mV*x(n) + 40 mV*x(n-1) + 20 mV*x(n-2) for a fixed pseudo-random symbol sequence that also covers the two symbols before t = 0, so the first two decisions see uncancelled intersymbol interference. Three disturbances of 85 to 95 mV against the symbol cause wrong decisions whose feedback propagates into the next decisions.

name: long-tr
purpose: tr = 1 ns, the longest legal transition, on a 50 ps grid (finer than tr/4), 3 ns clock, tap codes 2/1. Two resets rise 0.6 ns after a decision, while the outputs are still moving: the decision and the metrics reverse toward their cleared values, or keep falling past or short of their old targets. A decision turned against the raw input by the feedback feeds the next correction. A reset held to the end with one edge in reset.

name: min-pulse-vss-low
purpose: vss at the lower end of its range (-0.5 V) with vdd 1.5 V, the largest legal swing (2.0 V), and the shortest legal clk threshold pulses: one high time and one low time of 0.502 ns between vth crossings (the 0.5 ns minimum plus a 2 ps design margin, since a separation exactly at a minimum is a tie); also a 0.502 ns rst pulse and one pair of rising clk crossings 2.01 ns apart. vcm 0.55 V above vth 0.3 V, tap_lsb 40 mV, tr 40 ps on a 10 ps grid (tr/4), 90 ps control edges. Each output-changing event sits at 0.9 of the grid, so a scored row lies 1.275*tr after it. Power-up with tap codes 3/1; feedback of 40 to 120 mV turns decisions against the raw input, and the same input gives different decisions after different histories; the codes change to 1/2 between edges; a reset rises between edges and spans one edge while the codes change to 2/3; the first two decisions after it; the short reset pulse between two edges and the first two decisions after it.
